title: Quietly Steamed Malaysian Flour Dumplings
description: A traditional Malaysian dish featuring fermented and aerated flour dumplings, steamed to perfection in leaf wraps, perfect for a romantic dinner
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, yeast, and salt, and mix well.
Gradually add in the warm water, and mix until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes, until it becomes elastic and smooth.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it ferment in a warm place for 2 hours.
Punch down the dough, and divide it into 8-10 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball, and then flatten it slightly into a disk shape.
Place a tablespoon of coconut milk in the center of each disk, and fold the dough over to form a half-moon shape.
Wrap each dumpling in a pandan leaf, and place it in a steamer basket.
Steam the dumplings over boiling water for 15-20 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
Serve the dumplings warm, with a drizzle of sugar and vegetable oil.
